title: Protocol for enrichment, purification, and cytocentrifugation of mouse liver endothelial cells
protocol: Dissociate collagenase-digested mouse liver by gentle pipetting.
Filter through a 40 μM filter into a 50 mL conical tube.
Fill the 50 mL conical tube with RPMI 1640 media.
Spin at 60 × g for 2 min at 4°C.
Carefully collect the supernatant and transfer it to a new 50 mL conical tube using an automatic pipettor.
Repeat steps #1 and #2 at least three times to remove nearly all hepatocytes.
Centrifuge NPC-containing supernatant at 400 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Create Percoll gradients by layering 25% Percoll solution over 50% Percoll solution, if not already done.
Discard the supernatant after the 10-min centrifugation in step #4.
Resuspend LEC-enriched pellet in 3.3 mL of RPMI 1640 by gentle pipetting.
Carefully layer the 3.3 mL of resuspended cells in RPMI 1640 on top of the 25% Percoll layer.
Centrifuge gradient at 900 × g for 20 min at RT (20–22°C). Set brake to 0.
Set the Beckman Coulter Allegra 6 Centrifuge at room temperature (RT) between 20-22°C.
Ensure the brake is set to 0 before starting the centrifuge to prevent disruption of the gradient.
Centrifuge the sample according to the protocol for Percoll gradient separation.
Carefully remove and discard Layer #1 after the gradient spin, as it contains hepatic stellate cell-enriched population.
Collect Layer #2, which is LEC-enriched NPCs, into a 50 mL conical tube.
Collect Layer #2 into a new 50 mL conical tube on ice.
Add RPMI 1640 to fill up the 50 mL conical tube containing the collected LEC-enriched NPCs.
Spin at 550 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Discard supernatant and minimize any disruption of the pellet.
Resuspend pellet in 1 ml of RPMI 1640 for counting.
Pipette 1 million cells from each sample into one well of a 96-well U bottom plate.
Create wells for unstained and single-color controls.
Spin plate at 300 × g for 2 min at 4°C.
Discard supernatant by flicking the plate.
Prepare Fc Block working solution by diluting 1:100 in FACS buffer.
Resuspend cells in 25 μL of Fc Block working solution.
Pipette up and down several times.
Incubate on ice for at least 10 min.
Add 150 μL of FACS buffer to each well to wash Fc Block.
Spin plate at 300 × g for 2 min at 4°C.
Discard supernatant by flicking the plate.
Resuspend pelleted cells in 25 μL of antibody mix.
For unstained sample, and DAPI control sample suspend in 25 μL FACS buffer.
Pipette up and down minimum 5 to 6 times to ensure cells are evenly stained.
Incubate for 20 min on ice in the dark (container should be covered with lid or aluminum foil).
Add 150 μL of FACS buffer to each well to wash the cells.
Spin plate at 300 × g for 2 min at 4°C.
Discard supernatant by flicking the plate.
Resuspend cells in 200 μL FACS buffer, and transfer to a 5 mL polystyrene round-bottom tube.
Add 1 μL of DAPI (1:100 dilution) to DAPI-single color control well and experimental samples approximately 5 min prior to FACS.
Perform cytocentrifugation to mount sorted DAPI-, CD45-, CD31+ LECs onto slides for immunofluorescence or confocal microscopy examination.
Prepare all cytocentrifugation buffers and recipes on the day of the experiment before starting the protocol.
Spin sorted LECs at 550 × g for 7 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend sorted LECs in an adequate volume aiming for a final concentration of 50,000–70,000 cells per 100 μL.
Circle the bottom of the slide with a sharpie or hydrophobic pen to mark where the cells will be found after they are spun onto the slide.
Place cytology funnel (cytofunnel) against pre-coated slide.
Gently pipette the cell suspension of 100 μL into the cytofunnel after both the funnel and slide are secured with the cytoclip, and insert into metal cytocentrifugation apparatus.
Centrifuge at 800 RPM for 3 min.
Carefully retrieve the slide from the cytocentrifuge by lifting the slide straight up.
Fix with 4% PFA (50–100 μL /slide) at RT (20–22°C) for 15 min.
Wash slides 3× with 1× PBS for 5 min in Coplin jars. After each 5-min wash, remove excess fluid.
Quench the aldehydes with 50 mM ammonium chloride solution at RT (20–22°C) for 10 min.
Wash slides 3× with 1× PBS for 5 min in Coplin jars. After each 5-min wash, remove excess fluid.
Permeabilize slides with 0.1% Triton in 1× PBS at room temperature for 15 minutes.
Wash slides 3 times with 1× PBS for 5 minutes each in Coplin jars.
Block in 10% FBS in 1× PBS at room temperature for 1 hour.
Dilute primary antibody in blocking solution.
Incubate the diluted primary antibody 8–12 hours at 4°C or for 2 hours at room temperature.
Wash slides 3 times with 1× PBS for 5 minutes each in Coplin jars.
Dilute secondary antibody in blocking solution to desired concentration.
Stain the slides for 1 hour at room temperature under aluminum foil cover over a humidifying chamber.
Wash slides 3 times with 1× PBS for 5 minutes each in Coplin jars.
Locate cells on the slide.
Cover the cells with a cover slip.
Avoid air bubbles near the cells when placing the cover slip.
Seal the edges of the coverslip with clear nail polish to prevent displacement during imaging.
Image the slides as soon as the coverslips are dried.
Store sealed slides at 4°C and protected from light for up to one week if immediate imaging is not possible.
